meta.ogTitle: The Firefox Send alternative — encrypted, link-based, free

hero.title: The Firefox Send alternative
hero.body: Firefox Send was the simple, private way to share a file with an encrypted link — until Mozilla shut it down in 2020. BIShare brings that back: files are end-to-end encrypted in your browser, shared with a link that auto-expires, and never tied to an account. It also does something Firefox Send never could — send device to device instantly when you're on the same network.

why.title: What happened to Firefox Send?
why.body: Mozilla discontinued Firefox Send in September 2020 after it was abused for malware, and never brought it back. That left a gap: a dead-simple, end-to-end encrypted, no-account way to send a file with a link. BIShare fills it — the encryption key lives in the link fragment and never reaches our servers, so we only ever store ciphertext, exactly the model Firefox Send used.

0.b: Turn on end-to-end encryption and the file is encrypted before it leaves your device. The key travels in the link's #fragment, which browsers never send to a server — so we store ciphertext we can't read.

1.b: Share a link, QR code, or 6-character code. The recipient opens it in any browser and downloads — no account, no install. Links auto-expire after 24 hours instead of lingering in the cloud.

2.b: On the same Wi-Fi, BIShare sends the file straight between devices, end-to-end encrypted, with no upload at all — something Firefox Send never offered.

comparison.title: Firefox Send vs WeTransfer vs BIShare

0.q: What is the best Firefox Send alternative?
0.a: BIShare. It matches the thing people loved about Firefox Send — end-to-end encrypted file sharing through a simple, account-free link that expires — and adds instant nearby device-to-device transfer on top.

1.a: No. Mozilla permanently discontinued Firefox Send in 2020 and has said it won't return. If you're looking for the same encrypted-link experience, BIShare is the closest replacement.

2.q: Is BIShare really end-to-end encrypted like Firefox Send?
2.a: Yes. The file is encrypted in your browser with a key that rides in the link fragment and never reaches our servers, so we only store ciphertext. Nearby transfers are encrypted device-to-device and never touch the cloud at all.

3.a: No. You can send and receive without signing up. You just share a link, QR code, or 6-character code, and the recipient opens it in any browser.

4.q: How large a file can I send?
4.a: Encrypted share links carry files up to 100 GB free. For nearby device-to-device transfers over your own Wi-Fi there's no size cap, because nothing is uploaded to a server.
